title: A per-user rate limiter (token bucket)

authoring.author: Parikshaa content team
authoring.originality: Written for Parikshaa: our own rate limiter design case and kata, examples, code, quiz and explanations; no text from any site, book or course.

scenario: The placement portal's mock-test API is being hammered by a few students' scripts that submit answers in loops, slowing it for everyone. Design and code a per-user **rate limiter**: each student may make short bursts of requests, but over time no more than a fixed rate. Requests arrive with a timestamp in whole seconds.

clarifying_questions.a: Per user: one noisy student must not affect others.
Yes, up to a capacity, after which requests are refused until tokens refill.

clarifying_questions.q: What happens to a refused request?
clarifying_questions.a: It is denied immediately (HTTP 429 in the real API); it is not queued.
Yes, every request carries the current time in whole seconds, never going backwards.

clarifying_questions.q: Does a brand-new user start full?

functional: Configure capacity and refill rate once
Allow or deny each request per user, reporting tokens left
Refill lazily from timestamps, never above capacity

non_functional.name: Memory
non_functional.target: one small record per active user

entities.name: TokenBucket
entities.responsibility: Holds tokens, capacity, refill rate and the last refill time for one user; refills lazily and takes a token.

entities.name: RateLimiter
entities.responsibility: Maps users to buckets, creating a full bucket for a new user, and answers allow/deny.

entities.name: Driver (Main)
entities.responsibility: Parses commands and prints results; holds no limiting logic.

patterns.name: Lazy evaluation (refill on demand)
patterns.why: Instead of a timer adding tokens every second for every user, compute the refill from the time gap when a request arrives: O(1) and no background work.

patterns.name: Factory on first use
patterns.why: The limiter creates a bucket the first time a user appears, so configuration lives in one place.

diagram.alt: Class diagram: RateLimiter has a map from user to TokenBucket; TokenBucket has capacity, refill, tokens and last, with a tryTake method.

data.source:
classDiagram
  class RateLimiter {
    capacity
    refill
    buckets: Map~user, TokenBucket~
    allow(user, now)
  }
  class TokenBucket {
    capacity
    refill
    tokens
    last
    tryTake(now) bool
  }
  RateLimiter o-- TokenBucket

kata.io_protocol:
| Command | Prints |
|---|---|
| `LIMIT <capacity> <refill per second>` | `limit <c> per user, refill <r>/s` (once) |
| `REQ <user> <t>` | `allow <user> (<tokens left> left)` or `deny <user>` |

Before LIMIT: `error: no limit set`. A second LIMIT or anything else: `error: bad command <line>`. Timestamps are whole seconds and never decrease for a user.

rubric.criterion: Kata tests pass in the chosen language, including the change request.
Entities are separated: bucket logic in TokenBucket, user mapping in RateLimiter, parsing in the driver.
Refill is computed from timestamps on demand, capped at capacity; no timers.
The VIP change touches the limiter's bucket creation and the driver, not the bucket algorithm.
Naming, small methods and explanation (AI feedback, advice only).

concept_checks.stem: Capacity 3, refill 1 per second. A user makes 3 requests at t = 0 and 1 at t = 0. What happens to the 4th?
concept_checks.explanation: The bucket started with 3 tokens; the 4th request at the same second finds 0.

concept_checks.stem: Capacity 3, refill 2 per second. The bucket is empty at t = 0. How many tokens at t = 5?
concept_checks.explanation: 5 × 2 = 10 would be added, but the bucket is capped at 3.

concept_checks.stem: Why compute refill from timestamps instead of a timer that adds tokens every second?
options: It is O(1) per request with no background work for idle users
concept_checks.explanation: Lazy refill does work only when a request arrives.

concept_checks.stem: Which algorithm allows short bursts while keeping a long-run average rate?
concept_checks.explanation: Tokens accumulate up to the capacity, which is the allowed burst.

follow_ups: How would you share limits across several API servers (a shared store, atomic scripts)?
How would you compare token bucket with a sliding window log?
How would you return a Retry-After header?

revision_card.back: tokens = min(capacity, tokens + (now - last) × refill); last = now; if tokens == 0 deny; else tokens -= 1 and allow. Bursts up to capacity, long-run rate = refill. O(1), no timers.
